subject: Feature Fuse: Upgrade to Throughput + Bundling Qs
messages:
From: Jason Miller <jason.miller@brightlinelabs.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on tier moves + feature bundles

Hi Maya,

We're starting to see sustained traffic that makes the Compact plan a choke point for our LLM features. Nina and I discussed moving BrightLine to a throughput-focused tier but we're wrestling with how feature bundling works across tiers — particularly the realtime KV cache add-on and priority routing.

Two quick Qs:
- If we upgrade mid-term, do feature entitlements (KV cache, priority routing) carry over or do we need to purchase them separately?
- Can you outline the cost delta if we keep Compact seats + add KV cache vs switch to Throughput tier with KV included?

I've attached a short usage export (lightly redacted) — shows token distribution, p95 latency goals, and our typical concurrency. Would appreciate a short call next week to walk the proposal.

Thanks,
Jason
CTO, BrightLine Labs

Attachments: BrightLine_usage_summary.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Jason Miller <jason.miller@brightlinelabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on tier moves + feature bundles

Hi Jason — thanks for the data, this is helpful. Short answers up front:
- Entitlements: when you upgrade to Throughput, included features in that tier (e.g., standard KV cache) become available immediately; paid add-ons purchased under Compact don’t auto-refund but can be consolidated into the Throughput SKU under a credit conversation.
- Cost delta: depends on steady-state throughput and latency SLOs. From a quick look at the CSV, the break-even seems to be ~120M tokens/month. Below that, Compact seats + add-ons may be cheaper; above it, Throughput is more predictable and cheaper per token.

Cc'd Karthis (karthik_iyer) for a sizing check and Lauren (lauren_bishop) for pricing/credit options. Can we do a 30-min call Wednesday 9/13 10:00am PT? If that works I’ll share a sketch of two paths (consolidation vs hybrid).

Best,
Maya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | maya@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, Jason Miller <jason.miller@brightlinelabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on tier moves + feature bundles

Quick sizing note from my side after a skim of the usage CSV:
- Typical concurrency spikes to ~110 live requests; median sequence length ~480 tokens, p95 ~2.1k.
- If BrightLine keeps the Compact seat model + KV add-on, expect higher variability in latency under burst — KV add-on helps but batching limits still matter.
- Throughput tier with the higher GPU pool and prefix caching reduces token cost by ~22% in our projection and should hit your p95 latency target more consistently.

I'll prepare 2 numerical scenarios for the call: (A) Compact + KV (current) with projected overage pattern and (B) Throughput consolidated SKU with included KV and priority routing.

—Karthik, Solutions Engineering
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Jason Miller <jason.miller@brightlinelabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on tier moves + feature bundles

Thanks all — call was useful. Follow-up items that I promise to put in writing:
1) Two paths:
   - Path A (Hybrid): Keep Compact seats for core devs, purchase KV cache add-on and priority routing add-on. Estimated incremental ARR = $28,500/yr + variable token overages.
   - Path B (Consolidate to Throughput): Move to Throughput tier (3x current seat-equivalent) with KV & priority routing included. Estimated list ARR = $85,000/yr but unit token cost drops ~22% which yields ~30% lower expected monthly bill at current volumes.
2) Credit mechanics: We can apply a partial credit for unused Compact seat commitments toward the first 6 months of Throughput billing (subject to legal/finance approval). I’ve attached a proposed SKU matrix that shows the consolidation math.
3) Next steps: finance wants an estimated committed volume if you favor Throughput (helps speed approval). Jason — if you can confirm a 3- or 6-month commit estimate I’ll draft the quote and loop Legal for a short amendment.

Attachments: Proposed_SKU_matrix_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)

Cheers,
Lauren
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Miller <jason.miller@brightlinelabs.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on tier moves + feature bundles

Appreciate the clear options — leaning toward Path B (Consolidate to Throughput) because we need consistent p95 and simpler ops. Two action items from our side:
- I’ll confirm a 6-month committed token estimate by end of day Monday (9/15).
- Please include the partial credit language and a short clause that ensures included KV cache performance targets (p95 cache hit and latency) as a service expectation in the amendment.

If you can draft the preliminary quote and amendment language I’ll fast-track internal approval.

Thanks,
Jason
